newsitem.title: USA: Mubarak to ask Clinton to pressure Israel.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak to ask Clinton to pressure Israel.

text.p: President Hosni Mubarak said on Sunday he would ask President Bill Clinton to use his influence to pressure Israel into reversing its decision to build 6,500 Jewish homes in East Jerusalem.
"I'm going to ask the president to use his influence to stop this," he said on CNN's "Late Edition With Frank Sesno" programme.
"He could persuade the Israelis that this could cause problems in the future," Mubarak said ahead of a meeting with Clinton at the White House on Monday.
"It's going to make complications for the negotiations in the future and it will be a big problem," Mubarak said.
He also warned that the Israeli action could spark a flare-up of violence.
"It may reach that," he said. "I'm concerned with the stability of the area."

Mubarak was speaking in the wake of Israeli decisions to build 6,500 new Jewish homes in East Jerusalem and close down four Palestinian offices there. The moves have infuriated the Palestinians and irritated the United States.

Mubarak criticised a U.S. veto of a United Nations Security Council resolution that would have rebuked Israel for its decision, saying "it will create a feeling of injustice" in the Arab world and cause the United States to lose credibility.

The Egyptian leader is the latest in a procession of Middle East leaders to come to Washington. Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have both visited recently and King Hussein of Jordan is due this month.
